text:
alex_cust: Hey, hitting a weird streaming issue from our mobile SDK. Final JSON object is truncated ~50% of the time when users background the app and then re-open. No finish_reason, and client parse fails. Seen on iOS 16 and Android 13.

maya_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro curl or SDK snippet and any server logs you have? Does this happen with hosted API or a private deployment?

alex_cust: Hosted API. Repro steps: 1) Start a streaming chat request from mobile. 2) Background the app for ~10-30s while stream is ongoing. 3) Bring app to foreground -> SDK reconnects and tries to resume. Often the last chunk is missing (truncated JSON).

alex_cust: Here's the exact curl we've been using to emulate client resume (we're using event-stream SSE emulation):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -N -d '{"model":"gpt-like","stream":true,"prompt":"long output"}' https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/streams/chat
```

alex_cust: Observed server stream tail before reconnect:
```sse
data: {"delta":"Here is some text","index":17}

data: {"delta":"More text","index":18}
```
Then after reconnect, client shows: "...","index":19

maya_support: Thanks — can you share the raw bytes from the last SSE frame(s) or any HTTP proxy between mobile and our API? Also: are you using token rotation on the client?

alex_cust: Logs attached (pasted):
```
[mobile-proxy] 12:03:11 GET /v1/streams/chat 200 chunked
[sse] chunk 1 bytes=512
[sse] chunk 2 bytes=256
[sse] chunk 3 bytes=12  <-- looks like a tiny final chunk, content: "},"
[client] parse error: unexpected end of JSON input
```
We're rotating short-lived tokens every 20s (refresh flow). The SDK tries to resume by issuing a new request with resume headers when connection is lost.

sanjay_oncall: FYI we've seen Fastly/edge buffering + client reconnection cause the final SSE event to be lost on mobile background/resume patterns. If the client reconnects quickly, buffers can get dropped or interleaved.

maya_support: Two parallel ask: (1) can you reproduce with a non-rotating long-lived token to rule out auth handshake mid-stream? (2) enable verbose client keepalive and turn on SSE comments (":keepalive\n\n") so the connection isn't considered idle by intermediate proxies.

alex_cust: Will try long-lived token now. Quick test: with long token the failure rate drops to ~5% from ~50%. So token rotation likely exacerbates it. Still see some truncation on heavy network churn.

maya_support: Ok that's useful. For immediate mitigation: - increase client reconnection backoff to avoid racing the proxy, - add SSE heartbeat comments every 15s, - if you must rotate tokens, pause rotation while a stream is active or use a refresh token flow that doesn't terminate the underlying TCP.

alex_cust: Any server-side suggestions? We can't change network stack on millions of mobile devices.

sanjay_oncall: On the server/runtime side we can do two things: (A) ensure the runtime sends an explicit final sentinel event object (e.g., data: {"done": true, "finish_reason":"stop"}) and flush it aggressively with a tcp push. (B) improve resume semantics: when client resumes and requests a resume offset, the platform can attempt to re-emit the last N tokens as a safety net (idempotent re-send window). I'll open an infra task to evaluate feasibility.

maya_support: Filed internal ticket INFRA-11532 to explore aggressive final flush + resume window. In the meantime please try the client mitigations and confirm.

alex_cust: Trying heartbeat + longer backoff now. If we still see truncation I'll share pcap/samples. Thanks for quick triage. :+1:

infra-bot: INFRA-11532 created by sanjay_oncall: "Investigate SSE final flush and resume re-emit window to reduce truncated final-chunk on mobile reconnect". Priority: P2.

maya_support: Closing loop — if you can capture one full pcap showing truncated tail, upload to this thread and we'll attach to INFRA-11532. Also include client SDK version and whether using our hosted region proxied through any CDN.

alex_cust: Will do. SDK v2.4.1, users in us-west, behind standard CDN. Uploading pcap as soon as reproduce. Thanks everyone.
